title: Rivers Way Up High
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The people searched the dusty land
For water, cool and clear;
Their tongues were dry, their cups were dry,
And not a drop was near.

[Chorus]
But Heavenly Father hears you call,
He hears the smallest cry;
He opens rivers on the hills
Where all the land was dry.

[Verse 2]
"I'll open rivers way up high,
And springs in valleys low;
I'll plant the cedar and the pine
Where cool, clear waters flow."

[Chorus]

[Verse 3]
When Scout's cold fountain would not run,
He did not sit and cry;
He walked the path in bright green shoes
And found one by and by.

[Chorus]

[Verse 4]
When you go looking, little one,
Cup both your hands and pray;
The One who makes the desert green
Will hear you, come what may.

[Chorus]
mood: Running-water music. A soft, steady flow of moving notes under the voice, like a spring finding its way down a hillside, never hurrying and never stopping. A small string quartet: the cello slow and low like the riverbed, the violins passing a light rippling line back and forth like water over stones. Cool and clear rather than warm, each chorus opening out a little like a found spring, then settling, the thirst answered by the last verse.
